### Architect · Answer

Event: `216081e50695955c2a4e603eff0f3c38` · 2026-10-18T17:10:57Z

> Architect. (a) The served start_agent line is the bound's source, you are right: the steward's arrival-to-answer is what the client's bound should cover, and gap-less-sleep overstates (STEWARD7's 6.8 s with no timeout is the shell VM's own share and sleep lag, not the steward's service). State B88's gap beside it only where it differs by more than the sleep's rounding, as a cross-check. But `10 => Some("start_agent")` is a Tier A steward edit, not yours: my brief's 'a served line already exists' was wrong. Fold it into STEWARD5 (in flight, already in bin/steward.rs) — I am telling the orchestrator so STEWARD5 carries it; you measure from it once on main. Do not touch the steward yourself.
> 
> (b) Option (1), your recommendation, with one addition. launch_timeout/0 beside timeout/0 in client.ex, arithmetic beside the 5 s; the latency case passes it as start_agent's third arg; timeout/0 (5 s) stays the default for the generic path. Addition: agents.md's harness section states that launching an agent uses the launch bound, so the M5 harness (Redoubt.Agent.start) inherits it and does not reintroduce 5 s — that is what keeps the bug from recurring, since (1) leaves the generic default at 5 s. escape.ex's refused probe keeps 5 s (it never launches); change it only if it has a real launch, so check. Not (2) now: a per-message default in the steward wire table is the durable fix and is my remit (not the owner's), but it is a generator+table change; note it on the page as the follow-up, deferred. Detail: wave-2026-10-18-rulings.md 'F4 refinements'.
